# Initial rates: examples/rates/puromycin.csv

## Verdict

- [treated] Michaelis-Menten: the data give no evidence of substrate inhibition (p = 1) or cooperativity (Hill, p = 0.146).
- [treated] Substrate inhibition with Ksi above 4.13 ppm is not excluded; rates at [S] approaching that would show it or rule it out.
- [treated] Michaelis-Menten: Vmax 201.7 (174.2 to 232.6 counts/min/min), Km 0.05127 (0.03421 to 0.0754 ppm) (95% profile intervals).
- [untreated] Michaelis-Menten: the data give no evidence of substrate inhibition (p = 1) or cooperativity (Hill, p = 0.0844).
- [untreated] Substrate inhibition with Ksi above 3.82 ppm is not excluded; rates at [S] approaching that would show it or rule it out.
- [untreated] Michaelis-Menten: Vmax 150.1 (128.5 to 175.1 counts/min/min), Km 0.03617 (0.02188 to 0.05736 ppm) (95% profile intervals).
- Between groups: Vmax differs between treated and untreated: sharing it fits worse than separate values (F(1, 11) = 9.34, p = 0.0109).
- Between groups: Km: no difference between treated and untreated detectable by these data (F(1, 11) = 1.56, p = 0.237); the shared fit gives Km = 0.04423 (0.03241 to 0.05957). Not detected is not the same as equal.

## The data

23 rate(s) at 12 distinct condition(s) (11 replicate row(s)), in 2 groups by 'state': treated (12), untreated (11).
Units: substrate in ppm (not convertible to molar: fitted as given, and not comparable with a cited constant); rate in counts/min/min (an arbitrary unit: fitted as given).
Uncertainty: pooled from 11 replicate set(s): coefficient of variation 0.129 (11 degrees of freedom), scaled by each condition's mean rate.
One error estimate is pooled across all groups' replicates, which assumes every group was measured with the same precision.

## Michaelis-Menten (treated)

`v = Vmax [S] / (Km + [S])`

| constant | estimate | standard error | 95% profile interval | unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax | 201.7 | 12.71 | 174.2 to 232.6 | counts/min/min |
| Km | 0.05127 | 0.008623 | 0.03421 to 0.0754 | ppm |

- Chi-square 10.3 on 10 degrees of freedom, with sigma pooled from replicates (11 degrees of freedom). Most of that chi-square is the replicate scatter sigma was estimated from, so it is not a test; the lack-of-fit F test is.
- Correlations of the estimates: Vmax-Km +0.807.
- Starts: 6 of 6 reached this minimum; no start found a different one.
- Condition number of the weighted Jacobian (log constants): 4.95.
- Lack of fit: lack of fit F = 0.523 on 4 and 6 degrees of freedom, p = 0.724: no departure from this law's shape beyond the replicates' own scatter.
- Substrate range: Your 6 substrate concentration(s) span 0.39 to 21 times Km (below Km: 1; above: 5; in the guideline range of 0.2 to 5 times Km: 4). The Assay Guidance Manual asks for 8 or more in that range, with several on each side of Km.
- Substrate range: The range does not bracket Km. Eight concentrations evenly spaced on a log scale from 0.2 times the lowest to 5 times the highest Km in its interval would satisfy the guideline wherever Km lies: 0.0068, 0.012, 0.022, 0.038, 0.068, 0.12, 0.21, 0.38 ppm.

## The laws tested (treated)

| restricted law | general law | restriction | kind | statistic | p | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| michaelis-menten | substrate-inhibition | Ksi -> infinity | boundary (50:50 mixture) | F(1, 11) = 0 | 1 | not ruled out |
| michaelis-menten | hill | n = 1 | interior | F(1, 11) = 2.448 | 0.146 | not ruled out |

Ruled out means p below 0.05, a convention; every p-value is printed so another can be applied. A boundary restriction (a constant going to infinity) is tested against the 50:50 mixture of chi-square(0) and chi-square(1) (Self & Liang 1987): half the ordinary p-value.


Substrate inhibition (Haldane), for comparison (`v = Vmax [S] / (Km + [S] + [S]^2 / Ksi)`):

| constant | estimate | standard error | 95% profile interval | unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax | 201.7 | 12.71 | 174.2 to 244.8 | counts/min/min |
| Km | 0.05127 | 0.008623 | 0.03421 to 0.0791 | ppm |
| Ksi | not determined | - | > 4.125 (no upper bound) | ppm |

Ksi ran to the edge of the search; the standard errors above are conditional on it being held there, so they can understate the uncertainty the profile intervals beside them show.

- Ksi > 4.125 ppm: the data do not determine an upper bound. No substrate inhibition is detectable in this range; it would show at [S] approaching 4.13 ppm or above.

Hill, for comparison (`v = Vmax [S]^n / (K0.5^n + [S]^n)`):

| constant | estimate | standard error | 95% profile interval | unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax | 241.8 | 43.64 | 181.9 to 752.4 | counts/min/min |
| K0.5 | 0.09062 | 0.05569 | 0.03867 to 10.78 | ppm |
| n | 0.715 | 0.1709 | 0.3626 to 1.133 | - |

## Michaelis-Menten (untreated)

`v = Vmax [S] / (Km + [S])`

| constant | estimate | standard error | 95% profile interval | unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax | 150.1 | 9.967 | 128.5 to 175.1 | counts/min/min |
| Km | 0.03617 | 0.007218 | 0.02188 to 0.05736 | ppm |

- Chi-square 7.183 on 9 degrees of freedom, with sigma pooled from replicates (11 degrees of freedom). Most of that chi-square is the replicate scatter sigma was estimated from, so it is not a test; the lack-of-fit F test is.
- Correlations of the estimates: Vmax-Km +0.810.
- Starts: 6 of 6 reached this minimum; no start found a different one.
- Condition number of the weighted Jacobian (log constants): 5.52.
- Lack of fit: lack of fit F = 1.42 on 4 and 5 degrees of freedom, p = 0.349: no departure from this law's shape beyond the replicates' own scatter.
- Substrate range: Your 6 substrate concentration(s) span 0.55 to 30 times Km (below Km: 1; above: 5; in the guideline range of 0.2 to 5 times Km: 3). The Assay Guidance Manual asks for 8 or more in that range, with several on each side of Km.
- Substrate range: The range does not bracket Km. Eight concentrations evenly spaced on a log scale from 0.2 times the lowest to 5 times the highest Km in its interval would satisfy the guideline wherever Km lies: 0.0044, 0.008, 0.014, 0.026, 0.048, 0.087, 0.16, 0.29 ppm.

## The laws tested (untreated)

| restricted law | general law | restriction | kind | statistic | p | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| michaelis-menten | substrate-inhibition | Ksi -> infinity | boundary (50:50 mixture) | F(1, 11) = 0 | 1 | not ruled out |
| michaelis-menten | hill | n = 1 | interior | F(1, 11) = 3.597 | 0.0844 | not ruled out |

Ruled out means p below 0.05, a convention; every p-value is printed so another can be applied. A boundary restriction (a constant going to infinity) is tested against the 50:50 mixture of chi-square(0) and chi-square(1) (Self & Liang 1987): half the ordinary p-value.


Substrate inhibition (Haldane), for comparison (`v = Vmax [S] / (Km + [S] + [S]^2 / Ksi)`):

| constant | estimate | standard error | 95% profile interval | unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax | 150.1 | 9.967 | 128.5 to 180.4 | counts/min/min |
| Km | 0.03617 | 0.007218 | 0.02188 to 0.05856 | ppm |
| Ksi | not determined | - | > 3.816 (no upper bound) | ppm |

Ksi ran to the edge of the search; the standard errors above are conditional on it being held there, so they can understate the uncertainty the profile intervals beside them show.

- Ksi > 3.816 ppm: the data do not determine an upper bound. No substrate inhibition is detectable in this range; it would show at [S] approaching 3.82 ppm or above.

Hill, for comparison (`v = Vmax [S]^n / (K0.5^n + [S]^n)`):

| constant | estimate | standard error | 95% profile interval | unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax | not determined | - | > 138.6 (no upper bound) | counts/min/min |
| K0.5 | not determined | - | > 0.02738 (no upper bound) | ppm |
| n | not determined | - | < 1.083 (no lower bound) | - |

- Every substrate concentration is well below K0.5: there the Hill law is v = (Vmax/K0.5^n)[S]^n, so only n and the combination Vmax/K0.5^n act on these rates, and neither Vmax nor K0.5 alone is determined. K0.5 > 0.02738 ppm: the data do not determine an upper bound; Vmax > 138.6 counts/min/min: the data do not determine an upper bound. No interval is given for Vmax/K0.5^n, because its exponent n is itself fitted, and none for Vmax/K0.5, which these data do not determine unless n = 1.
- n < 1.083: the data do not determine a lower bound.

## Between groups (Michaelis-Menten)

| shared constant | statistic | p | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax | F(1, 11) = 9.345 | 0.0109 | differs |
| Km | F(1, 11) = 1.565 | 0.237 | no difference detected |
| all | F(2, 11) = 7.31 | 0.00956 | the groups differ |

- Vmax differs between treated and untreated: sharing it fits worse than separate values (F(1, 11) = 9.34, p = 0.0109).
- Km: no difference between treated and untreated detectable by these data (F(1, 11) = 1.56, p = 0.237); the shared fit gives Km = 0.04423 (0.03241 to 0.05957). Not detected is not the same as equal.

The fit with Km shared:

| constant | estimate | standard error | 95% profile interval | unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax [treated] | 192.9 | 10.2 | 170.4 to 217.6 | counts/min/min |
| Vmax [untreated] | 158.7 | 8.491 | 140.4 to 178.7 | counts/min/min |
| Km | 0.04423 | 0.005676 | 0.03241 to 0.05957 | ppm |

## What these numbers are

- FITTED to this file's rates, under the law named, not measured constants: their provenance is this dataset and this law, and they are conditional on both.
- Intervals are 95% profile-likelihood intervals (Bates & Watts 1988); the standard errors are asymptotic and are what a +-2 SE interval would be built from, which for Km is often too symmetric.
- A fit this good is not evidence that the law is right; the tests above compare the laws fitted, and a law not fitted was not considered.
- References: Cornish-Bowden A. Fundamentals of Enzyme Kinetics, 4th ed. Wiley-Blackwell, 2012 (rate laws). Segel IH. Enzyme Kinetics. Wiley, 1975 (inhibition laws). Bates DM, Watts DG. Nonlinear Regression Analysis and Its Applications. Wiley, 1988 (profile intervals). Self SG, Liang KY. J. Am. Stat. Assoc. 82:605 (1987) (tests on the boundary). Draper NR, Smith H. Applied Regression Analysis. Wiley (lack of fit and pure error). Hurvich CM, Tsai CL. Biometrika 76:297 (1989) (AICc). Brooks HB et al. Basics of Enzymatic Assays for HTS. Assay Guidance Manual, NCBI Bookshelf NBK92007 (the 0.2-5 Km design range).
